chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Buffalo 1928 band personnel: Jack Butler not Jack Sprat, Bill Howard on drums
summary: Going through the listed personnel, Horace identifies trumpeter Jack Butler instead of 'Jack Spratt', notes four saxophones including Joe Thomas, and drummer Bill Howard from Columbus.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Great. Okay, here we're talking about the stompers again. This is 1928 when you left Pittsburgh and you had the engagement at the Paramount Claremont Inn in Buffalo. I'm assuming that that's 1928. They have that in quotes here, but according to the -- this piece here, it says, "I suspect that Jack Spratt, who was listed as one of your trumpets, along with Roy Eldridge and Red Harland," says, "I suspect that Jack Spratt and Sprat Morton are not the same man or that there is a mixup between the original notes and the topography." So that's correct. Jack Spratt is somebody different?
Okay, because you indicated -- or it's indicated here that Sprat Morton -- that Roy took Sprat's --
-- his place, so he would have not gone on to Buffalo --
-- with you. Do you recall Jack Sprat? It's even possible that that was a fake name for somebody.
It could have been. I had a Jack Butler with me, not a Jack Sprat, and we called him Tonics. And he was a great guy, and he was crippled fellow.
It was during that era. Yes.
Those were the trumpets -- Roy Eldridge, Red Harland and Jack Sprat. Then Russell Bowles and Archie Hall were the trombones, Van Sherrill, Cleve Mack were alto --
I don't know how they left him out.
They don't have him listed either this time.
Uh-huh. Yeah, that would seem strange you'd have two altos and one tenor.
Yeah, right, Wait a minute, I (unintelligible).
Banjo -- they have it listed as guitar. And Bill Howard is drums. Who did you say before?

Do you know, that is correct. Bill Howard -- he was out of Columbus, Ohio. Instead of Jimmy King. Jimmy King preceded Bill Howard. That's correct, Bill Howard, little short guy out of Columbus, Ohio, Bill Howard. That is correct.
Okay, so Bill Howard probably again was on that job in Columbus. Maybe you picked him up there or something.
